question.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 3\}$
and has mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{9}xy,$ where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters. The moment of inertia of the plate about a line $l$ perpendicular to the plate is $\frac{13}{4}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.$
Given that the center of mass of the plate is at $(2,2),$ find the distance of the line $l$ from the center of mass.
question.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

First, we find the mass of the plate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{9}xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{|}_{0}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot \frac{9}{2}\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}\,\text{kg}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular line through the center of mass $(2,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{M} & ={∬}_{D}((x-\overset{―}{x})^{2}+(y-\overset{―}{y})^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}((x-2)^{2}+(y-2)^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}((x-2)^{2}+(y-2)^{2})\cdot \frac{1}{9}xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}x(x-2)^{2}y+x{y}^{3}-4x{y}^{2}+4xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{[\frac{1}{2}x(x-2)^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}-\frac{4}{3}x{y}^{3}+2x{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+\frac{9}{4}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{8}{x}^{4}-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{9}{8}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{81}{8}-18+\frac{81}{8} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the parallel axis theorem and solving for $d,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M \\ \frac{13}{4} & =\frac{9}{4}+\frac{9}{4}{d}^{2} \\ \frac{9}{4}{d}^{2} & =1 \\ {d}^{2} & =\frac{4}{9} \\ d & =\frac{2}{3}\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$
